DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Nobody Ships a Feeling

STS-HS10-L4-13001400-HSSCIENG910-PCI-GBL-01 • HS Science: Engineering Design 9–10 • Defining Criteria and Constraints
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Engineers who design for the whole world write two lists before they build anything. One list says what the design must do. The other list says the limits it has to stay inside, written in numbers. The blue drum on this show has to roll over rough roads in four countries, fit through the narrowest door, and cost less than thirty dollars.
One team wants to add the words easy to push to the brief. What number could you add so that a tester could measure it?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Amara doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what Amara is doing with exact evidence. Use precise words, not "stuff."
2
What is Deven holding?
Look at the picture. Justify what Deven holds and how it relates to the design being judged. Name it exactly.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what the teacher is doing and what he is testing. Use exact numbers from the picture.
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Justify what place this is with at least two exact clues.
5
Tell me about the design brief board.
Look at the picture. Justify how the board would settle a disagreement about the design. Use exact terms.
6
What is Nadia wearing?
Look at the picture. Justify Nadia's role from her clothing and what she holds. Be precise.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: HS-ETS1-1 — Analyze a major global challenge to specify qualitative and quantitative criteria and constraints for solutions. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
